web.lane: Data-integration / iPaaS field-to-field mapping UX research — Zapier, Make, Workato, Segment, Tray.io, Boomi (+ n8n as a relevant comparable). Focus: the visual mapping step (source→destination binding), transforms, defaults/fallbacks, validation, unmapped-field handling, and live-sample previews. Goal: a concrete recommendation for how VenueOS should let non-technical operators bind live data sources (POS, score feeds, calendars, weather, SIS) to template widget fields inside its Canva-style editor.

products.name: Zapier (Send data between steps / Zap action fields)
products.mappingApproach: The lowest-floor, most non-technical pattern. There is NO drag-line canvas. Each destination field is a normal form input; you click into it and a dropdown drops down listing every field available from prior steps. Picking a field inserts it inline as a labeled colored TOKEN/PILL (e.g. a green 'Order ID' chip) that sits inside the text box, so a field can mix static text + multiple pills ('Order ID: {pill}'). Source fields come entirely from the SAMPLE/TEST DATA captured on the trigger step — Zapier shows the real sampled value next to each option so the operator recognizes what they're picking. If an expected field isn't in the sample, the workaround is 'custom pill mapping' (manually type the field reference) plus re-testing the trigger to refresh the field list. Type-matching is the operator's responsibility (date field needs a date value, number field needs digits with no '$'). Static/default values are entered by just typing into the field instead of inserting a pill. Takeaway: dropdown-of-pills + inline tokens + sample-value-next-to-each-option is the canonical pattern for the least technical audience. Sources: help.zapier.com 'Send data between steps by mapping fields', 'Enter data in Zap fields'; community.zapier.com 'custom pill mapping', platform.zapier.com 'Add input fields'.

products.name: Make (Integromat) — mapping panel
products.mappingApproach: Click a destination field and a mapping PANEL opens on the right with a data tree of every upstream module's output; you drag (or click) an item into the field and it becomes a colored TOKEN/pill that can be combined with literal text ('Order ID: {token}'). The panel is TABBED: tab 1 = mappable data items from prior modules; the remaining tabs are function libraries grouped by category (general, math, text/binary, date/time, array, custom) so transforms live in the SAME picker as fields — you compose 'formatDate({pill}; ...)' visually. Outputs are 'bundles' (JSON objects); operators learn that one module's bundle feeds the next module's inputs. There is also a per-field 'map' toggle that flips a structured dropdown into free-map mode so you can map a dynamic value into a field that would otherwise force a fixed picklist choice. Takeaway: tokens + a single panel that unifies field-picking AND transform functions behind tabs. Sources: help.make.com 'Mapping', 'Step 8. Map data', make.com 'Use functions', community.make.com 'What does the Map toggle do?'.

products.name: Workato — datapills + datatree
products.mappingApproach: 'Datapills' are the unit of mapping: each is an output variable from the trigger or a prior action, shown in an expandable DATATREE ('Recipe data' section). You DRAG a pill from the datatree into an input field; a field accepts pills (variables), constants (typed literals), or a blend of both in one field. Crucially the datatree shows SAMPLE DATA pulled from the connected account in italics next to each pill, so operators see real values before running. 'Formula mode' on a field unlocks Ruby-style transforms (to_currency, to_date, to_i, to_s, .pluck, .to_json) for power users — but it's an opt-in mode, not the default surface. Two standout non-technical features: (1) TOGGLE FIELDS — a picklist normally renders a dropdown that can't accept a pill; toggling it to plain-text mode lets you map a pill in; (2) GROUP/AUTO data mapping — auto-maps fields when the destination field NAME matches a datapill name, which collapses large schemas (DB tables) to one click. Hidden/unmapped fields are reachable via bracket notation on a parent pill (Params['C']). Takeaway: sample-data-in-the-picker + name-based AUTO-MAP + an opt-in formula mode that keeps the default surface simple. Sources: docs.workato.com 'Datapills and fields mapping', 'Group Data Mapping'.

products.name: Segment (Twilio) — Destination Actions mapping
products.mappingApproach: Closest model to 'bind an event/source to a system field.' Per destination action you get a mapping editor with two source tabs — 'Event Variables' (incoming source properties) and 'Enrichments' (previously-configured derived data). The editor SHOWS REQUIRED FIELDS AUTOMATICALLY and hides optional ones behind a '+' ('The required fields appear automatically. Click + to see optional fields') — a strong progressive-disclosure pattern. You can 'Select Object' to pass a whole object or 'Edit Object' to map each property individually. Destination fields support DOT NOTATION to build nested output ('info.name', 'info[0].email'). Transforms are first-class (coalesce, case conversion, JSON encode, flatten, string replace, concatenate). Static values are typed via dedicated tabs for string/boolean/number/null. The killer trust feature: a 'Send test event' step runs your real sample event through the mapping and shows the LIVE MAPPING OUTPUT rendered in the destination's exact format, so you validate before going live. Coalesce IS the default/fallback primitive. Takeaway: required-first progressive disclosure + a live 'what the destination will actually receive' preview from a real sample event. Sources: twilio.com/docs/segment 'Destination Actions'; segment.com/docs/connections/destinations/actions.

products.name: Tray.io — embedded end-user Config Wizard (most relevant to VenueOS)
products.mappingApproach: Tray runs TWO surfaces: a power-user drag-and-drop workflow builder (Data Mapper connector with 'Map one value' / 'Map object to list' ops, dynamic output schemas), AND a deliberately dumbed-down EMBEDDED Config Wizard for non-technical end users. In the wizard, mapping is reduced to a 'Field List' — a simple list/dropdown of fields per service — where the end user just picks source field → destination field; all builder complexity (connectors, test data, expressions) is HIDDEN. Schema can be supplied four ways so the dropdowns are never empty: partner-defined (hardcoded by Tray for messy/nested connectors), automatic schema detection (dropdowns auto-pull field names from the connector op), dynamic lookup generation (fields change based on a prior selection — e.g. Account vs Lead record type re-derives the available fields), and config-slot values from custom code. Takeaway: the single most important lesson for VenueOS — separate a SIMPLE embedded picker (dropdown of fields, zero expressions) from the power builder, and pre-populate the dropdowns by auto-detecting the connector schema so a non-technical user never faces a blank field. Sources: tray.ai/documentation embedded 'Intro to data mapping', 'End-user defined schema', 'Determining input schema', 'Tray partner-defined schema'.

products.name: Boomi — Map component (classic ETL drag-line, power-user end of spectrum)
products.mappingApproach: The most technical, most visual model: a two-column canvas with the SOURCE PROFILE tree on the left and DESTINATION PROFILE tree on the right. You map by clicking a source element and DRAGGING A LINE to a destination element; a visible connector line is drawn between them. Profiles (XML/JSON/CSV/flat-file) are explicit schemas you define first as 'blueprints.' Transforms are FUNCTION STEPS placed BETWEEN the two columns — you wire source → function (string ops, concat, date/time, math) → destination, and can chain/order functions. Connection rules encode validation: a source can fan out to many functions/destinations, but each destination element accepts only ONE inbound connection (prevents value conflicts). Default values cover both unmapped cases: applied when source is null/blank, OR applied always when a destination field has no source mapping at all. Takeaway: the drag-line + two-column + functions-in-the-middle metaphor is powerful and self-documenting but assumes schema literacy — it's the WRONG default for VenueOS's audience, though its default-value and one-inbound-connection rules are worth copying. Sources: help.boomi.com 'Map components', 'Mapping elements from source to destination'; community.boomi.com.

products.name: n8n (relevant comparable — drag-from-INPUT-pane)
products.mappingApproach: A three-view INPUT pane (Schema / Table / JSON) sits beside the node; you DRAG a value from the input pane onto a field and n8n auto-generates the underlying expression for you (so non-technical users get expression power without writing syntax). 'Schema view' shows a simplified structure from the first item; Table/JSON show the full dataset. 'Data pinning' freezes a real sample so you can build the whole mapping against known values without re-running upstream nodes — and 'Schema Preview' lets you map against a node's expected output BEFORE it has ever executed (solves the empty-dropdown cold-start). Takeaway: drag-to-generate-expression + pin-a-sample + schema-preview-before-first-run directly address the 'I can't map what I haven't fetched yet' problem. Sources: docs.n8n.io 'Referencing data in the UI', 'Schema preview', 'Data mapping in the expressions editor', blog.n8n.io 'data pinning & mapping'.

uxPatterns: DROPDOWN-OF-FIELDS over drag-lines for non-technical users. Zapier, Workato, Segment, and Tray's embedded wizard all default to 'click the field → pick from a list.' Drag-a-line-on-a-canvas (Boomi) is reserved for ETL power users and assumes schema literacy. The two-column drag-line is impressive in a demo but is the wrong default for a non-IT operator.

INLINE TOKEN / PILL representation. A mapped field renders the bound source as a colored, labeled chip embedded in the input (Zapier green pills, Make colored tokens, Workato datapills). This lets one field MIX static literal text with one or more dynamic bindings ('Order ID: {pill}', 'Welcome {firstName}!') and makes the binding visible/removable at a glance.

SAMPLE / LIVE DATA SHOWN IN THE PICKER ITSELF. Every best-in-class tool shows the actual sampled value next to each selectable field (Zapier test-record values, Workato italic sample data, n8n input pane). The operator recognizes 'home_team = Lincoln HS' instead of guessing what a cryptic field name means. This is the single biggest comprehension lever.

LIVE OUTPUT PREVIEW from a real sample BEFORE going live. Segment's 'Send test event' renders the mapping result in the destination's exact format; n8n pins sample data; MapForce/Informatica preview the transformed output. 'Show me exactly what the screen/widget will display with today's real data' is the trust-builder that turns a config form into something an operator will sign off on.

PROGRESSIVE DISCLOSURE: required fields first, optional behind a '+'. Segment surfaces only required mappings and hides optional ones behind a click. Reduces a 40-field schema to the 3 things that actually must be bound — critical for a non-technical operator's 30-second happy path.

AUTO-MAP BY NAME MATCH. Workato's group data mapping auto-binds when a destination field name matches a source field name; Tray auto-detects connector schema to pre-fill dropdowns. The app does the obvious mappings itself and only asks the human about ambiguous ones — the 'app almost does the work for them' principle.

DEFAULT / FALLBACK VALUE as a first-class field option, with two distinct modes: (a) use default when the mapped source is null/blank (Boomi, iPaaS.com), and (b) set a constant with no mapping at all (Boomi 'no source → always default'). Coalesce (Segment) is the same idea as a transform. Every robust mapper has an explicit 'if empty, show this' so a screen never renders a blank or 'undefined'.

TRANSFORMS LIVE IN THE SAME PICKER, TABBED/OPT-IN. Make puts function categories (date, text, math, array) as tabs in the same mapping panel; Workato gates Ruby formulas behind an opt-in 'formula mode'; Segment offers named transforms (case, coalesce, concat, format). The default surface stays a simple picker; power is one click deeper, never in your face.

DRAG-TO-GENERATE-EXPRESSION. n8n lets users drag a value and writes the expression for them — expression-language power without making a non-coder type syntax. A middle path between rigid dropdowns and a raw formula box.

COLD-START / EMPTY-DROPDOWN MITIGATION. n8n 'schema preview' (map before the node has ever run) and 'data pinning', plus Tray's partner-defined/auto-detected schema, all solve 'I can't bind a field I haven't fetched yet.' Provide a predeclared schema and/or a cached sample so the picker is never empty on first use.

PICKLIST↔FREE-MAP TOGGLE. Workato toggle fields and Make's 'map' toggle let a field that normally forces a fixed dropdown choice instead accept a dynamic binding. Needed whenever a field is sometimes a constant pick and sometimes data-driven.

VALIDATION VIA TYPE-MATCH + CONNECTION RULES. Zapier warns date/number type mismatches; Boomi enforces one inbound connection per destination element (no silent overwrite); Segment requires required fields before enabling. Validate at bind-time, in plain English, not at run-time with a stack trace.

UNMAPPED-FIELD HANDLING IS EXPLICIT, NOT SILENT. Best practice (iPaaS.com, Tackle, Boomi): for an unmatched destination field, offer 'skip' (leave clean), 'set default', or 'leave for later' — never let an unmapped field silently produce a blank/error downstream. Surface the count of still-unmapped fields.

DOT-NOTATION / NESTED PATHS for advanced shapes. Segment destination fields accept 'info.name' / 'info[0].email'; Workato reaches hidden fields via Params['C']. Useful escape hatch, but kept out of the default flow.
keyTakeaways: Two distinct audiences need two distinct surfaces. Every mature platform that serves non-technical users (Tray embedded, Workato, Segment Actions, Zapier) offers a SIMPLE dropdown-of-fields picker AND a power-user expression/formula mode — the simple one is the DEFAULT and the power one is opt-in. The pure drag-line ETL canvas (Boomi) is a power-user-only tool and converts poorly for non-IT operators.

Drag-a-line-between-two-columns LOOKS like the obvious 'mapping' metaphor but is actually the most technical, lowest-conversion choice for non-technical users. The winning pattern for that audience is: click a destination field → dropdown of source fields (each showing its live sample value) → pick → it becomes an inline pill.

Showing real sample/live data — both in the field picker AND as an end-to-end output preview before go-live — is the highest-leverage comprehension + trust feature. It is what separates 'a scary config form' from 'I can see exactly what my screen will show.' VenueOS already has live preview infrastructure (the template editor renders widgets), so this is a natural strength to lean into.

The app should do the obvious mappings automatically (name-match auto-map à la Workato, schema auto-detect à la Tray) and only ask the human about ambiguous or required-but-missing fields. This is the same 'Integration Concierge / the app almost does the work for them' north-star already in VenueOS's CLAUDE.md.

Defaults/fallbacks and unmapped-field handling must be EXPLICIT and first-class. A signage screen rendering 'undefined' or a blank price in front of customers is a brand-damaging failure mode; every robust mapper has a per-field 'if empty, show this' plus an explicit skip/default choice for unmapped fields. This is more important for live customer-facing screens than for back-office iPaaS.

Transforms belong in the same picker, one layer deep, tabbed and opt-in (Make's tabbed function panel is the model) — never a mandatory formula box on the default path. Most VenueOS bindings are 1:1 (score → score, item name → text); formatting (currency, date, uppercase) covers ~90% of the rest and can be preset chips, not free-text code.

Progressive disclosure (required-first, optional-behind-+, à la Segment) is essential to hit VenueOS's standing '30-second happy path' acceptance gate — an operator binding a menu board should see 3 required fields, not a 40-field POS schema.
web.venueOsRecommendation:
Build a 'Bind to live data' picker that lives INSIDE the Canva-style template editor's Properties panel — not a separate iPaaS canvas. Concretely:

1) SURFACE & ENTRY POINT. Next to every editable widget field in PropertiesPanel (the same place StyleableField/ExternalHtmlTextEditor already render), add a small data-plug/lightning icon. Clicking it flips that single field from 'static value' to 'bound to a source,' mirroring Workato's toggle-field and Make's 'map' toggle. The default editing surface stays exactly what operators already know (type a value); binding is one opt-in click deeper. This keeps the per-field mental model and avoids a scary standalone mapping screen.

2) DROPDOWN-OF-FIELDS, NOT DRAG-LINES. The picker is a searchable dropdown grouped by connected source (Toast POS, Square Catalog, the score feed/CTS bridge, Google Calendar, weather, Clever/SIS, sponsor manager). Each entry shows the field name AND its current live sample value pulled from that integration ('home_score → 21', 'item.price → $12.99', 'menuItem.is86 → false'). This is the Zapier/Workato pattern and it is by far the highest-comprehension choice for the non-IT operator (AD, restaurant manager, church admin) VenueOS targets. Reserve any drag-line/two-column UI ONLY for an optional advanced view; do not make it the default.

3) RENDER BINDINGS AS INLINE PILLS. A bound field shows a colored chip ('{Home Score}') and supports mixing literal text + multiple pills in one field ('{awayTeam} @ {homeTeam}', '{itemName} — {price}'). This reuses the token concept from Zapier/Make/Workato and makes bindings visible and removable.

4) AUTO-MAP ON CONNECT (the Concierge moment). When an integration connects (e.g. Toast), and the operator drops the matching vertical template (Menu Board), auto-bind every field whose name/role obviously matches (item name→TEXT, price→price field, image→IMAGE) — Workato group-mapping + Tray schema-auto-detect. Show a one-line summary ('We auto-filled 9 of 11 fields — 2 need your input') and only prompt for the ambiguous/required-missing ones. This is the literal realization of VenueOS's Integration Concierge vision and its 30-second happy path.

5) LIVE OUTPUT PREVIEW — your unfair advantage. Because the editor already renders widgets live, render the widget WITH REAL SAMPLE DATA from the source the instant a binding is made (Segment 'send test event' / n8n pinned data, but for free). The operator literally watches the menu board fill with today's actual prices, or the scorebug show the live score. Add a 'preview with sample data' toggle for sources that aren't live yet (n8n schema-preview pattern) so the picker is never empty before the first real feed arrives — predeclare each connector's schema + a canned sample.

6) DEFAULT / FALLBACK PER FIELD — mandatory for customer-facing screens. Every bound field gets an explicit 'If no data, show: ___' (Boomi/Segment-coalesce pattern). A signage screen must NEVER render 'undefined', a blank price, or a stale score. For auto-86 / sold-out, bind to a boolean and offer a preset behavior ('hide row' / 'show SOLD OUT'). Surface a count of any still-unmapped required fields and block 'publish' until they're defaulted or bound (Segment required-first gating).

7) TRANSFORMS AS PRESET CHIPS, ONE LAYER DEEP. Cover the 90% with named, no-code format chips on the binding (Currency, Uppercase, Title Case, Date format, Round, Truncate) — Make's tabbed-function panel and Segment's named transforms, minus the code. Gate any raw expression/formula box behind an 'Advanced' affordance for the rare power user (Workato formula-mode pattern). Most VenueOS bindings are 1:1 and need zero transform.

8) RESPECT THE EXISTING ARCHITECTURE. Bindings should resolve through the same signed Redis pub/sub fan-out that already pushes content to the player fleet (so a price/score change propagates in real time and survives the offline-first cache), and every bind/unbind of a data source should write an AuditLog row (consistent with the Standard Audit Surface). Treat a bound widget exactly like any other widget for scheduling, RBAC, and Taurus/Chromium-83 rendering rules.

Net: copy Zapier/Workato/Tray's dropdown-of-fields + inline-pills + live-sample-in-picker, copy Segment's required-first + live-output-preview + coalesce-default, copy Tray/Workato's auto-map, and explicitly REJECT Boomi's drag-line canvas as the default. VenueOS's differentiator is that its template editor already does WYSIWYG live rendering — so the 'live output preview' that costs Segment a dedicated test step is essentially free, and it should be the centerpiece of the experience.

web.lane: Competitive UX research: how leading digital-signage CMS products bind template widget fields to live data sources, and a concrete field-to-system mapping recommendation for VenueOS.

products.name: OptiSigns (OptiSync — Dynamic Data Mapping)
products.mappingApproach: The gold-standard, WYSIWYG drag-drop binding model and the closest analog to a Canva-style editor. (1) DATA SOURCE FIRST: operator adds a DataSource from Account Settings OR from inside the Designer app. Sources: Google Sheets, Excel Online, CSV, JSON, XML, REST API (via 'API Gateway'), POS (Toast/Square/Clover via API), HRIS/inventory, Zapier (6,000+ apps). (2) BIND IN DESIGNER: a 'DataSource' panel appears in the Designer left side-menu listing the source's rows/columns. Operator expands 'Row 1' and DRAGS a column-field (or a whole row) onto the canvas; a pop-up asks 'Would you like to use this data in a Repeater or on its Own?'. Standalone fields bind one value to one element. (3) PER-ELEMENT BINDING: select any text box or image element, click Settings, open the 'Value' menu, pick the correlating column name (pulled from the DataSource). Image elements bind to an image-URL column. (4) REPEATER: a side-menu tool with ready-made 'Repeater components' + 'Repeater Templates'; double-click opens the Repeater Editor; edit one card and it replicates the design across every row in the dataset (rows → repeating cards). (5) POS MENU-BOARD SPECIFICS: item name + price columns map to text elements; an 'available' boolean column drives conditional Sold-Out badges / strike-throughs (available=false → sold-out=1). (6) AUTO-REFRESH: 'set it and forget it' — source change propagates to every screen with no manual republish. Tagline: 'change content once, change it everywhere.'

products.name: Rise Vision
products.mappingApproach: Component-with-config-fields model (no free-canvas drag-bind). Operator drops a purpose-built COMPONENT into a Presentation placeholder, then configures it: the Google Spreadsheet / List component takes a pasted 'Spreadsheet Key' + a 'Select Worksheet' dropdown; the rise-financial component exposes named instrument fields (lastPrice, netChange, name, percentChange). Two data-management modes: AUTO-SYNC (link a Google Sheet/CSV → component auto-renders the rows) or MANUAL (click into each field to type, 'Add Row', drag-handle reorder, trash-icon delete, paste HTTPS image URL or pick from Rise storage). 'Placeholder' in Rise = a layout container for a content playlist, not a merge field. Editing requires the 'Content Editor' role. Strength: friendly for non-technical K-12 staff; weakness: binding is component-scoped, not arbitrary-element-scoped.

products.name: ScreenCloud (Dashboards)
products.mappingApproach: Embed-the-dashboard model — NO field-level mapping. Operator connects a data source ONCE via credentials/OAuth (Power BI, Tableau, Salesforce, Looker Studio, Zendesk, Jira, GitHub, Grafana, Trello). ScreenCloud renders the live dashboard in the cloud and pushes a high-res view to the screen; multiple dashboards combine into a Playlist that rotates automatically. Security selling point: 'credentials never leave our secure cloud and never get exposed to screens.' This is BI-on-a-wall, not template-field binding — the operator never maps a column to a widget; the source tool owns the visual. Best for KPI/exec/ops use cases, not menu boards or scoreboards.

products.name: Yodeck
products.mappingApproach: App + Custom-App model. For data sources, operator creates an 'App' instance (Apps tab → Create App → pick Google Sheets / Smartsheet / Airtable / Salesforce → name it) — the app embeds the source (Google Sheets via published iframe; documented limitation: fixed frame size, no reflow, minutes-delayed republish). For true field binding Yodeck pushes operators to CUSTOM APPS: an uploaded HTML5/JS ZIP package (runs locally on the player) or a Web App (a URL automated via Yodeck's scripting engine), configured through a developer-authored 'UI Form Definition' that exposes config fields. So Yodeck's native no-code path is 'embed the source'; granular field-to-widget mapping is a developer/HTML-app task, not a drag-drop operator flow.

products.name: BrightSign (BrightAuthor / BrightAuthor:connected)
products.mappingApproach: Named-feed + bind-by-name model, player-centric. Operator defines a 'Data Feed' (RSS / MRSS / Dynamic Playlist) with a NAME and an Update Interval (how often the player re-polls the feed URL). To display it they add a 'Live Text' element (overlays dynamic/static text on an image/video in an interactive zone) or a Ticker zone, and bind it BY THE FEED'S NAME; Networked User Variables provide another live-text binding path. A 'Dynamic Playlist' widget points at an external content bucket and continuously re-checks it so layout stays fixed while content changes. Binding granularity is feed→zone/element, not column→element; it's the most technical/AV-integrator-oriented of the five and assumes a feed already exists.

uxPatterns: DATA-SOURCE-FIRST, THEN BIND: every product separates 'register a connection' (credentials/URL/Sheet key, done once, reusable) from 'bind a field to a widget' (done per template). VenueOS should model a first-class DataSource entity separate from the template.

TWO BINDING GRAMMARS — pick the WYSIWYG one: (a) DRAG-DROP VISUAL BIND (OptiSync, embed signage) where a fields panel lists columns and you drag one onto an element or pick it from a per-element 'Value' dropdown; (b) MERGE-TAG TEXT BIND where you type {{ColumnHeader}} into a text field (column header must EXACTLY match the tag name — the #1 failure mode). For a Canva-style editor the drag-drop/'Value'-dropdown model is the right fit; merge-tags can layer on top for power users.

THE REPEATER IS THE KEY PRIMITIVE for list/table data: design ONE card, bind its sub-fields to columns, and the engine replicates it for every row. This is how OptiSync turns a spreadsheet into a menu/roster/leaderboard without per-item design. It maps cleanly to VenueOS menu boards, sponsor rotations, and leaderboard-mode scoreboards.

BIND BOTH TEXT AND IMAGES: an image element binds to an image-URL column (logos, item photos, headshots); a text element binds to a string/number column. VenueOS already has StyleableField for text and asset/URL pickers for images — add a 'bind to data' affordance to both.

CONDITIONAL FORMATTING DRIVEN BY DATA: OptiSync's 'available' boolean → Sold-Out strike-through, and embed signage's condition rules (change text color / swap media when a value crosses a threshold). Essential for menu auto-86 and for sports (e.g., highlight the leading team). VenueOS should support per-element conditional rules keyed off a bound field.

POLL-INTERVAL / AUTO-REFRESH PER SOURCE: every product re-fetches on an interval (BrightSign explicit 'Update Interval'; OptiSync/embed configurable poll). The signage value prop is 'edit the sheet/POS, screens update themselves.' VenueOS already owns a signed pub/sub — push changes instead of poll for near-instant fan-out, a competitive edge.

CREDENTIAL ISOLATION: ScreenCloud's 'credentials never reach the screen' — the server holds the connection, the player only ever receives rendered/normalized data. Critical for POS/API keys; aligns with VenueOS's offline-first player that should get pre-normalized JSON, never raw API tokens.

FORMAT-AS-YOU-BIND: embed signage lets you format a bound field as text/number/currency/percentage/date/list/media at bind time. Menu prices, sports stats, and KPIs all need this; bake a format dropdown into the binding UI.

TEMPLATE-AS-SCHEMA REUSE: OptiSync's 'change once, change everywhere' — one bound template fed by per-location/per-device data (embed signage binds by Device tag) renders differently on every screen. Maps directly to VenueOS multi-location menu pricing and multi-school rosters from one template.
keyTakeaways: There are really only two operator-facing binding grammars in the market: (1) drag-drop / 'Value'-dropdown visual binding (OptiSync, embed signage) and (2) {{merge-tag}} text binding. Everyone else either embeds a whole external dashboard (ScreenCloud, Yodeck apps) or binds a named feed to a zone (BrightSign). For a Canva-style WYSIWYG editor, the visual drag-drop model is the only one that fits the metaphor.

OptiSigns/OptiSync is the clear product to beat on this axis — it is the only one offering true arbitrary-element-to-column binding inside a drag-drop designer, the Repeater for row-to-card replication, conditional Sold-Out logic, and broad source coverage (Sheets, Excel, CSV, JSON, XML, REST, Toast/Square/Clover, Zapier) in a no-code flow. VenueOS should treat OptiSync as the feature-parity baseline.

The Repeater (design one card → bind sub-fields → auto-replicate per row) is the single most important primitive to copy. It is what makes spreadsheet→menu-board, roster→leaderboard, and POS→pricing work without per-item manual design, and VenueOS has no equivalent today.

The universal failure mode of the merge-tag approach is name-mismatch (tag text must equal the column header character-for-character). A picker/dropdown that injects the exact field reference eliminates this entire support-ticket class — prefer click-to-bind over type-the-tag.

Separate the 'connection' from the 'binding': register a DataSource once (URL/Sheet key/OAuth/API), reuse it across many templates and elements. All five products enforce this split; it is also the right security boundary (keep POS/API credentials server-side, push only normalized data to players).

VenueOS already owns three assets none of these competitors fully have for this feature: a signed real-time pub/sub (push data changes to screens in ~150ms instead of polling), an offline-first player with pre-cache tiers (cache last-known data so a menu/scoreboard survives a network drop), and an AI Integration Concierge (auto-detect the source + auto-map columns to a seeded template). Combining drag-drop binding WITH these is the differentiated play, not just matching OptiSync.

Sports is a natural extension of the same machinery: a live ScoreSource (console tap-off / manual / league feed) is just another DataSource, the scoreboard is a Repeater-free single-row binding, and leaderboard-mode (track/swim/gymnastics) is exactly the Repeater pattern — so one binding engine serves both signage verticals and live sports.
web.venueOsRecommendation:
Build a ONE binding engine that serves signage and sports, modeled on OptiSync's drag-drop visual binding (the only paradigm that fits a Canva-style editor), then differentiate with VenueOS's existing pub/sub + offline cache + AI Concierge.

DATA MODEL (additive Prisma): a first-class `DataSource` entity {id, tenantId, type (GOOGLE_SHEET|CSV|JSON|XML|REST|POS_TOAST|POS_SQUARE|POS_CLOVER|SCORE_FEED), connectionConfig (encrypted — keys NEVER reach the player), schema (discovered column list + inferred types), pollIntervalMs, lastFetchedAt}. A `FieldBinding` on each TemplateZone/widget {sourceId, columnRef, format (text|number|currency|percent|date|image), fallback, conditionalRules[]}. Reuse the existing ScoreSource abstraction as a DataSource subtype so sports and signage share the engine. Keep credentials server-side and push only normalized JSON to screens (ScreenCloud's 'credentials never reach the screen' principle) — this fits the offline-first player perfectly.

BINDING UX (in the existing Canva-style editor): (1) DATA-SOURCE-FIRST — a 'Data' panel in the left rail (peer of the widget/variant panel) lists connected sources and their columns, with an 'Add data source' button that routes through the AI Integration Concierge (paste a URL / pick POS / paste a Sheet link → we discover + connect). (2) CLICK-TO-BIND, NOT TYPE-A-TAG — every text element (already StyleableField) and image element (already has asset/URL picker) gains a small 'Bind to data' chip; clicking opens a 'Value' dropdown of columns from a chosen source (OptiSync's exact model). This eliminates the merge-tag name-mismatch support class. Optionally still accept typed {{Source.Column}} for power users, but the dropdown is the default. (3) REPEATER WIDGET — the headline new primitive: drop a Repeater, bind it to a source, design ONE card with bound sub-fields, and it replicates per row. Ship ready-made Repeater templates per vertical (menu item, roster row, leaderboard line, sponsor tile). (4) FORMAT + CONDITIONAL RULES inline at bind time (currency for prices, an 'available=false → strike-through + Sold Out badge' rule for menus, 'leading team → highlight' for sports). (5) AUTO-REFRESH via the SIGNED PUB/SUB instead of polling — when a Sheet/POS/score changes, fan the new normalized data to every screen in ~150ms (a real edge over every competitor's poll loop), with the offline cache holding last-known values so a board never goes blank on a WiFi drop.

SEQUENCING: Phase 1 — DataSource entity + Google Sheet/CSV connector + per-element 'Value' dropdown binding (parity with the no-code baseline). Phase 2 — Repeater widget + conditional Sold-Out logic + POS connectors (reuse the existing Toast/Square/Clover work) for menu boards. Phase 3 — wire ScoreSource as a DataSource so the scoreboard/leaderboard widgets bind through the same engine; pub/sub push + offline last-known-value cache. Phase 4 — AI Concierge auto-mapping ('we found a price column and a name column — want a menu board?') and conversational 'build-it-for-me' template seeding. This collapses the IT-consultant step OptiSigns still requires for API setup and is the 30-second happy path the CLAUDE.md UX gate demands.

web.lane: Field-to-system mapping in live sports scoreboard / broadcast-graphics tools. Two architectural camps exist. (1) BROADCAST-GRAPHICS camp (Singular.live, vMix, Ross XPression, Chyron PRIME) — a designer builds a template, exposes specific element properties as NAMED, addressable handles ('control nodes' / 'mapped title fields' / 'DataLinq-bound objects' / table-column bindings), and a separate live feed pushes values into those named handles by matching field name. (2) SCOREBOARD/VENUE-CONTROL camp (Daktronics Show Control + All Sport + RTD, ANC LiveSync, CTS) — the raw scoring console emits a serial/UDP string, a 'template/definition file' DECODES that string into a CATALOG of named fields (home_score, inning, balls, strikes, clock, penalty...), and the operator maps catalog fields onto display zones. CTS is purely a SOURCE (9600-baud serial scoreboard protocol) feeding the Daktronics-style catalog pattern. The universal primitive across all seven products: a feed is decomposed into NAMED FIELDS, on-screen elements expose NAMED BINDABLE SLOTS, and mapping = associating the two — most powerfully via name-auto-match with manual override.

products.name: Singular.live (Composer + Control Nodes + Data Stream API)
products.mappingApproach: Designer-exposes-then-feed-pushes model. In Composer the designer clicks an UNDERLINED property on a widget (e.g. a Text element's 'Text' property), a Node Link Browser pops up, they type a NAME for the control field and click Add; the property turns green to confirm it is now an addressable 'control node'. Control nodes are then visible in the Data Interface / Control Panel where a human operator (Studio/UNO control app) OR an external system can set them. For LIVE data (clocks/scores at 1Hz+), a 'Data Stream' is created in Data Stream Manager, added to the composition, and CONNECTED to the matching control nodes; an external system PUTs/WebSocket-pushes JSON ({compositionName, controlNode, payload:{Time, Score_a, Score_b...}}) at sub-300ms latency, and each JSON key lands in the like-named control node. Net UX: name the slot on the graphic, push a JSON object keyed by those names. Account-global data nodes can drive many compositions at once.

products.name: vMix (Data Sources + Title Designer)
products.mappingApproach: Per-field column-mapping in a dialog. Operator opens the Title Editor, selects a Title FIELD from the left column (Headline, Description, Score, Clock...), clicks 'Data Source' in the top menu bar, then picks Data Source -> Table -> Column. The killer convenience is the COLUMN = 'Auto' default: vMix first matches by NAME (a column called 'Headline' auto-binds to the 'Headline' field), and falls back to INDEX matching (1st column -> 1st field) when no name matches — so a well-named sheet needs almost zero manual mapping. A Format string ('Name: {0}') wraps the raw value with static text. Sources are Google Sheets / Excel / CSV / XML / JSON / Text / web, with a configurable polling 'update interval' and an 'Auto Next' row-advance. Live scores are typically driven by a Google Sheet (or scoreboard-OCR/feed) that updates rows live; the bound title repaints on each poll.

products.name: Ross XPression DataLinq (+ DataLinq Server, ScoreBridge)
products.mappingApproach: Schema-binding model for enterprise broadcast. A DataLinq Server connects to a data SCHEMA — Excel/Tables, ADODB, any ODBC source (MS SQL, Access, MySQL, Firebird), XML, JSON, RSS/SMS, plus purpose-built scoreboard-vendor sources and the NFL GSIS format. The designer binds individual scene OBJECTS (text/material/image) to specific cells/fields/columns of that schema inside XPression Designer; at playout the live row drives the on-air graphic. Scoreboard data specifically arrives via connectors like ScoreBridge / the 'XPression DataLinq and Scoreboard Sources' app note, which read the scoring console and present clock/score/period/penalty as DataLinq fields. Visual Logic can add conditional formatting on top of the binding. Strength = arbitrary DB-grade schemas; cost = a designer/engineer sets up the binding, not a casual operator.

products.name: Daktronics Show Control + All Sport + RTD
products.mappingApproach: Decode-string-into-named-field-catalog model — the canonical scoreboard pattern. The All Sport console (3000/5000/5500) emits Real-Time Data (RTD): a packetized serial string (0x16-prefixed, checksum, 19200 8N1 over RS232) or via the All Sport CG / DSTI data hub re-broadcast over UDP. RTD is just text until a TEMPLATE FILE decodes it: Data Interface Definitions (DID, for DMP-8000) or Input Template Files (ITF, for DMP-7000) turn the raw stream into a CATALOG of named fields — e.g. baseball exposes home/away runs-hits-errors, inning line score, balls, strikes, outs, due-ups, pitch speed, etc. The operator then works in Content Studio: the DID's 'Name' column appears as Dynamic Data Library folders, and they DRAG/assign a named RTD field onto a display zone/element. A Data Monitor tool shows raw vs decoded fields for troubleshooting. The clock comes locally/fast from the console; the value-add is the field catalog + the visual zone editor.

products.name: ANC LiveSync
products.mappingApproach: Whole-venue-canvas, timeline + live-trigger model. LiveSync treats the entire venue (videoboards, ribbon/fascia, fixed displays) as ONE frame-accurate canvas over standards-based IP (NDI, SMPTE 2110). Content is template-based and scheduled on a 24/7 TIMELINE, with precision live-trigger control for in-game moments. Sports scoring, real-time stat feeds, social and emergency messaging are integrated data sources with built-in rendering; bound score/clock/stat values fan out to many surfaces simultaneously from a single control surface (used at Fenway, Dodger Stadium, Wells Fargo Center, Gainbridge Fieldhouse). The operator binds data into templated elements and triggers/schedules them across surfaces rather than mapping cell-by-cell; the differentiator is synchronized multi-surface playout, not the granularity of the field-map UI.

products.name: ChyronHego / Chyron PRIME 4.7 (incl. PRIME Scorebug)
products.mappingApproach: Table-Resource + group-level Parameters-Effect binding — explicitly built to AVOID cell-by-cell linking. PRIME's native Table Resource ingests CSV or hand-entered data, auto-detects column types, and shows an editable GRID inside PRIME Designer (league tables, rosters). The new 'Parameters Effect' binds an entire ROW of data to a scene at the GROUP level — multiple fields connect to multiple graphic elements in ONE action instead of manually linking each cell to each element. At playout the operator selects/ tabs a table row to populate and live-edit the on-air scene. For automated scorebugs, PRIME CG drives graphics from a sports-data web API so metrics (down, distance, yardage, player stats, clock) AUTO-BIND to visual elements by field. Built on the PRIME platform so the same assets serve scorebugs and full overlays.

products.name: Colorado Time Systems (CTS) integrations
products.mappingApproach: Pure SOURCE in someone else's mapping model — not a binding UI. CTS timing consoles emit a scoreboard protocol over serial (9600 baud, continuous, channel-byte-prefixed readout data, Gen6/legacy CTS vs Gen7/WA-2 variants) and can output RTD over UDP (port 3002). There is no CTS-native 'map a field to a graphic' editor; instead the CTS stream is consumed by a downstream system that DOES the mapping: Daktronics RTD (select 'Colorado Timer', COM/UDP, baud 9600) decodes it into the named-field catalog above, and third-party bridges (and community projects intercepting the scoreboard input) re-publish clock/lane/place/time/score as bindable fields for web scoreboards or broadcast tools. Lesson for VenueOS: CTS = the kind of feed you ingest and normalize into named fields, exactly like the project's existing CTS serial bridge.

uxPatterns: NAMED-FIELD as the universal primitive: every product decomposes a feed into named fields and exposes on-screen elements as named bindable slots. Mapping is just associating slot<->field by name. VenueOS should give every Sport's SportDefinition a canonical field vocabulary (homeScore, awayScore, period, clock, shotClock, balls, strikes, outs, possession, penalty...) and give every scoreboard widget a `boundField` property drawn from that vocabulary.

NAME-AUTO-MATCH WITH MANUAL OVERRIDE (vMix 'Auto' column) is the single highest-leverage UX: if the slot name equals the feed field name, bind automatically; only surface a picker when names don't match. This is the '30-second happy path' for field mapping — operator picks a sport, the scoreboard template's slots auto-bind to the live feed, zero manual wiring.

DESIGNER-EXPOSES-THEN-FEED-PUSHES (Singular control nodes): the person who builds the template decides which properties are data-addressable by clicking the property and naming it; the live feed (or operator console) then just sets named handles. Decouples template design from data wiring and lets one feed drive many boards. Maps cleanly onto VenueOS's Canva-style editor — clicking a field in PropertiesPanel and toggling 'Bind to live data' = creating a control node.

DECODE-STRING-INTO-CATALOG via template/definition files (Daktronics DID/ITF): raw console bytes are useless until a definition turns them into a human catalog. VenueOS's CTS/console bridge already does parsing; the product gap is exposing the parsed result as a BROWSABLE FIELD CATALOG (a 'Dynamic Data Library') the operator drags from.

GROUP / ROW-LEVEL BINDING IN ONE SHOT (Chyron Parameters Effect; vMix Auto-mapping): binding field-by-field doesn't scale to a full scoreboard. Offer a one-click 'bind this whole board to this feed' that maps every slot at once by name, with a diff view of any unmatched fields.

GRID/SHEET AS THE FALLBACK DATA SOURCE (vMix Google Sheets, Chyron Table Resource, XPression Excel): when there's no live console, a live-editable spreadsheet/grid is the universal manual feed. A polling interval + row-advance turns a sheet into a 'feed'. VenueOS should accept a Sheet/CSV as a ScoreSource so manual + console + API are interchangeable.

LIVE-EDITABLE GRID DOUBLES AS PLAYOUT CONTROL (Chyron tab-into-row, vMix click-a-row): the same grid that holds the data is the operator's run-of-show control — select a row to put it on screen. Unifies data entry and triggering.

SOURCE ABSTRACTION / INTERCHANGEABLE FEEDS (Daktronics 'select your timer', CTS-into-RTD): the binding layer is decoupled from the feed type — manual, serial console, UDP/RTD, web API, or sheet all present the same named fields downstream. Mirrors the project's planned ScoreSource abstraction.

POLLING-VS-PUSH LATENCY TIERING (Singular sub-300ms WebSocket for clocks vs vMix poll interval for slow data): clock/score need push-grade latency; rosters/standings can poll. VenueOS already has signed WebSocket pub/sub — route the clock through it and let slower fields poll.

FORMAT/TRANSFORM STRINGS ON THE BINDING (vMix '{0}', XPression Visual Logic): the bound value rarely renders raw — operators want prefix/suffix/conditional formatting ('Q{0}', 'Name: {0}', color-on-penalty) attached to the binding itself, not baked into the template.

TROUBLESHOOTING / RAW-VS-DECODED VIEW (Daktronics Data Monitor): a panel showing raw feed bytes next to decoded named fields is essential for setup and field support — the operator can SEE the feed is alive and which field is which.

ONE BINDING, MANY SURFACES (ANC LiveSync canvas; Singular account-global data nodes): bind once, fan the value to video board + ribbon + scorebug + stream overlay simultaneously. VenueOS's per-surface cue fan-out is the same idea — a bound score updates every surface from one source of truth.
keyTakeaways: The industry splits into two camps and VenueOS should deliberately fuse them: the BROADCAST-GRAPHICS camp (Singular/vMix/XPression/Chyron) is great at flexible designer-driven binding but assumes a broadcast operator; the SCOREBOARD/VENUE camp (Daktronics/ANC/CTS) is great at decoding real scoring consoles and fanning to many surfaces but uses engineer-grade config. VenueOS's wedge (Canva-style editor + signed pub/sub + existing CTS/console bridge) lets it offer the broadcast camp's binding ergonomics on top of the scoreboard camp's real console feeds.

The reusable primitive everywhere is NAMED FIELD <-> NAMED SLOT. There is no product where the operator wires raw byte offsets to pixels; every tool first decomposes the feed into named fields (Daktronics DID catalog, Singular JSON keys, vMix columns, Chyron table columns, XPression schema fields) and exposes graphic elements as named addressable slots, then matches them. VenueOS must formalize a per-sport canonical field vocabulary as the contract between SportDefinition, the scoreboard widgets, and every ScoreSource.

vMix's 'Auto' column-by-name match is the gold-standard low-friction UX and directly serves the project's 30-second-happy-path mandate: name the slots to match the feed and binding is automatic, with a manual picker only for mismatches. Combined with Chyron's group/row-level 'bind it all in one shot', the target UX is 'pick sport -> pick feed -> board auto-binds, here are the 2 fields I couldn't match'.

Singular's control-node flow (click an underlined property, name it, it becomes data-addressable) is the most natural fit for VenueOS's Canva-style PropertiesPanel: a 'Bind to live data' toggle on any text/number field that turns a static StyleableField into a named bindable slot. Static-by-default, data-driven-on-demand, same editor.

Daktronics RTD proves the value of a browsable FIELD CATALOG ('Dynamic Data Library' folders fed by the DID 'Name' column) plus a raw-vs-decoded Data Monitor. VenueOS already parses CTS/console serial in its bridge; the missing product surface is exposing those parsed fields as a draggable catalog and a live feed-health/raw-vs-decoded debug panel.

CTS is a cautionary data point: it has NO mapping UI — it is purely a serial source that downstream systems (Daktronics RTD, third-party bridges) decode and bind. VenueOS should treat every console (CTS Gen6/Gen7, Daktronics All Sport, OES, etc.) as an interchangeable ScoreSource that normalizes into the same canonical field vocabulary, so the binding UX is identical regardless of feed origin.

Latency must be tiered: Singular pushes clocks over a sub-300ms WebSocket while slow data polls; Daktronics keeps the live game clock local/fast from the console and pulls slower stats from the data hub. VenueOS should send clock/score through its existing signed pub/sub (push) and let rosters/standings/sponsor data poll — and follow the 'two clocks' rule (clock from local console, stats from lagging league feed, never mixed).

Bindings carry transforms, not just values: vMix format strings ('{0}'), XPression Visual Logic, and conditional formatting live ON the binding. VenueOS bindings need an optional prefix/suffix/format + simple conditional (e.g., flash on penalty, show only when shotClock>0) so the editor stays in charge of presentation while the feed supplies the value.

One binding -> many surfaces is a venue-grade expectation (ANC's single canvas, Singular's account-global data nodes). VenueOS's per-surface cue fan-out already matches this; the data layer should expose a bound field as a single source of truth that repaints video board + ribbon + scorebug + stream overlay together.
web.venueOsRecommendation: Build field-to-system mapping as a thin, name-based binding layer on top of three things VenueOS already has (the Canva-style template editor, the signed WebSocket pub/sub, and the CTS/console serial bridge). Concretely: (1) CANONICAL FIELD VOCABULARY — give every SportDefinition a fixed dictionary of named fields (homeScore, awayScore, period, clock, shotClock, balls, strikes, outs, possession, penaltyHome, penaltyAway, lane/place/time for leaderboard sports...). This is the contract; it mirrors Daktronics' DID field catalog and Singular's control-node names. (2) BINDABLE SLOTS IN THE EDITOR — add a 'Bind to live data' toggle on every numeric/text StyleableField in PropertiesPanel (Singular's underlined-property pattern). Toggling it turns the field into a named slot whose `boundField` is chosen from the active sport's vocabulary; static-by-default, data-driven on demand — fully consistent with the Canva-style editor and the project's editability standard. Attach optional format/transform to the binding (vMix '{0}' prefix/suffix + a simple conditional like flash-on-penalty / hide-when-zero). (3) SCORESOURCE ABSTRACTION normalizing every feed to that vocabulary — manual phone entry, CTS Gen6/Gen7 serial, Daktronics All Sport RTD, generic web/JSON API, and a live Google-Sheet/CSV (vMix-style polling) all emit the SAME named fields downstream, so the binding UX never changes with feed type; clock/score ride the existing signed pub/sub (push, sub-300ms) while rosters/standings poll, and enforce the 'two clocks' rule (live clock from local console, lagging stats from league feed). (4) AUTO-MAP-BY-NAME WITH OVERRIDE as the headline UX — when an operator picks a sport and a feed, every slot whose name matches a feed field binds automatically (vMix 'Auto'); offer a one-click 'Bind whole board to this feed' (Chyron Parameters/group binding) that maps all slots at once and shows a small diff of only the unmatched fields for manual picking. That is the sub-30-second happy path the project mandates. (5) FIELD CATALOG + FEED-HEALTH PANEL — a browsable 'Live Data' drawer (Daktronics Dynamic Data Library) the operator can drag fields from, plus a raw-vs-decoded debug view (Daktronics Data Monitor) showing the feed is alive and which byte is which field — essential for the water-polo/CTS install support burden. (6) ONE BINDING -> MANY SURFACES — a bound field is a single source of truth that fans to video board + ribbon + scorebug + stream overlay via the existing per-surface cue fan-out (ANC single-canvas / Singular global data node). Net: clone Singular's bind-by-clicking-a-property ergonomics + vMix's auto-match-by-name + Daktronics' field catalog + Chyron's group binding, sit it on the ScoreSource abstraction over the existing serial bridge, and route through the existing signed pub/sub — almost entirely assembly of parts VenueOS already owns, which matches the Sprint 13 'mostly assembly' thesis. Route operators who have a console/feed but don't want to wire anything through the Integration Concierge: detect the feed, auto-create the ScoreSource, auto-bind the scoreboard template, done.

web.lane: POS-to-template field mapping for digital menu boards — UX patterns across first-party POS-native, dedicated menu-first vendors, generic-signage data-binding layers, and enterprise QSR systems. Research basis: Square Kiosk/Square for Restaurants support docs; Toast direct-sync + 86 docs; Clover via Spectrio/SmarterSign/AIScreen; Yodeck DSMenu; Wallboard; Menuzen; Menuboard Manager; DSMenu; OptiSigns OptiSync Dynamic Data Mapping; Intuiface; Coca-Cola Cokesolutions QSR. Relevant to VenueOS tasks #198/#201/#208 (menu-management platform, per-location POS pricing, auto-86).

products.name: Square for Restaurants + Square Kiosk (first-party, POS-native)
products.mappingApproach: Zero field-mapping by design — the POS Item Library IS the schema, so there is nothing to bind. The operator works entirely inside Square: each Catalog item already carries name, price, photo, modifiers, and live availability. To put it on a customer-facing display the operator just (1) assigns the item to a Category and (2) toggles 'Show on Kiosk'. Photos auto-fill from the item's image; if a category has no image, Square automatically borrows an image from one of the category's items. Price/86-status flow straight from the register with no operator step. The 'template' is a fixed Square-controlled layout (category grids + item tiles), not a free-form canvas. Takeaway for VenueOS: the lowest-friction mapping is NO mapping — when you own (or fully mirror) the catalog, the UX is 'tag it to show, and it appears.' But you give up design freedom — Square's look is locked. Source: squareup.com/help articles 8312 (Edit Square Kiosk menus/items/categories), 8538 (Set up Square Kiosk), 6424 (Create menus with Square for Restaurants), 8553 (Manage menus across locations).

products.name: Toast POS (via Menuboard Manager, Wallboard, Checkmate direct-sync)
products.mappingApproach: Auto-import + zero per-field mapping; the differentiator is automatic 86/68 (out-of-stock) handling. Operator flow per Wallboard's published 6 steps: Connect (built-in API connector links the Toast account) -> Import (auto-pulls items, categories, pricing, AND modifiers) -> Design (drag-and-drop editor) -> Schedule -> Publish -> Monitor. The operator never maps name->name or price->price; the connector ingests Toast's menu tree wholesale. Toast's own item-availability state ('86 an item' on the POS or Toast Web) propagates so the board either hides the item or flips it to 'Sold Out' automatically, and restores it when back in stock. Modifiers come across too. Takeaway: at the dedicated-vendor tier, 'mapping' has collapsed into 'pick which Toast menu/section to mirror'; the field-level binding is implicit and vendor-maintained. Source: menuboardmanager.com/toast, wallboard.us/wallboard-toast-integration, support.toasttab.com '86 an Item', doc.toasttab.com Menu item inventory overview, support.itsacheckmate.com Toast POS Direct Sync.

products.name: Clover POS (via SmarterSign, Spectrio, AIScreen, Nento, NoviSign)
products.mappingApproach: Same auto-import model as Toast: 'after initial setup, users only maintain products and descriptions inside Clover, and menu boards update automatically.' The connector pulls item names, descriptions, prices, stock status, and modifiers live. No field-binding UI is exposed to the operator — the integration owns the schema map. The only operator decision is which Clover catalog/category to surface and which design template to drop it into. SmarterSign frames it as 'prices in your POS are automatically sent to your menus; inventory is represented automatically.' Takeaway: across Toast/Clover/Square the dedicated-vendor consensus is that field mapping should be INVISIBLE — the operator's mental model is 'my POS is the single source of truth; the board is just a skin.' Source: smartersign.com/clover, support.spectrio.com Clover Menu Boards Tutorial, aiscreen.io/apps/clover-digital-menus, nento.com/clover-digital-menu-board, novisign.com Clover POS integration.

products.name: Menuzen (menu-first signage, multi-location)
products.mappingApproach: Best-articulated 'item objects, not fields' model — the most directly copyable pattern for VenueOS. Operator can either sync the POS item database OR build their own item catalog in Menuzen, then 'drag and drop ITEMS onto the menu board canvas' (whole item objects carrying all their fields, not individual name/price fields). Three named features: (1) 'Intelligent Item Flow' — when an item is 86'd/unavailable at a location it is instantly removed and the layout closes the gap and reflows automatically (solves the dead-space problem auto-86 normally creates); (2) 'Multi-Location Toggler' — build once, deploy everywhere; Menuzen pulls store-specific pricing from the data source so one design renders different prices per store; (3) 'Smart Layouts' — adaptable designs that auto-adjust by rules you set (time-of-day, location) from a single file. Takeaway: this is the gold-standard target UX for a Canva-style editor — the operator manipulates first-class ITEM objects, the system handles fields + reflow + per-location price resolution. Source: menuzen.com.

products.name: OptiSigns OptiSync — Dynamic Data Mapping (generic signage with explicit binding)
products.mappingApproach: The clearest example of EXPLICIT, visible field-to-element binding — relevant because it shows how a general-purpose canvas editor (like VenueOS's) exposes mapping without code. Workflow: Connect a data source (POS API, Google Sheet, Excel, table) -> open the Designer template -> select ANY text box or image element -> open Settings and set its 'Asset Element Name' to a data field (e.g. bind a text box to item.name, another to item.price, an image element to item.photo) -> a 'Repeater' takes one designed row and repeats it for every row in the data source, turning a tabular menu into N rendered menu rows automatically. To verify/debug a binding the operator clicks a mapped element and opens Settings to see which field it's wired to. Marketed as 'map your API data directly onto your screens with our drag-and-drop designer' with auto-refresh on data change. Takeaway: when you DO want design freedom, the proven non-technical pattern is per-element binding via a Settings/properties panel + a Repeater for the list — exactly mappable onto VenueOS's PropertiesPanel + StyleableField. Source: support.optisigns.com articles 29217646663187 (Set Up Dynamic Data Mapping), 31860170199955 (POS menu boards with OptiSync), 31113088917907 (Toast API data), 22875592994195 (Integrate API via OptiSync); optisigns.com/product/optisync-dynamic-data-mapping.

products.name: Intuiface (no-code interactive/QSR signage)
products.mappingApproach: No-code binding layer aimed at 'creatives, not developers.' Uses an 'API Explorer' to connect back-office/cloud services and any Web API, plus a headless-CMS mode for managing public content from a browser. Binding is element-level (text/image elements bound to data) with collections/repeaters for lists, configured through the visual editor rather than code. Detail on the exact panel UX is thin in public docs (gated behind their Academy/400+ help articles), but the positioning confirms the same two-layer split: a connector for the data source + a visual editor where elements are bound to fields. Takeaway: reinforces that 'no-code field binding' is a recognized category, but the discoverability of the binding step is the hard UX problem these tools under-document. Source: intuiface.com/digital-menu-board-software, intuiface.com/blog How to Make a Digital Menu Board Interactive.

products.name: Enterprise QSR stack (Coca-Cola/Cokesolutions framing; Navori, LOOK, Pickcel, Lsquared)
products.mappingApproach: Centralized CMS owns the menu data model; the display is a rules-driven renderer. Operators rank Content Control (68%) and Pricing Flexibility (49%) as top needs and demand swap-by-daypart + rapid price/inventory edits. POS integration drives real-time price, automatic 86, and synchronized in-store + drive-thru boards; on top of the POS feed sits a DAYPARTING + RULES engine that swaps content by time-of-day, day-of-week, season, and local events/weather, with franchisee-level local overrides under brand-standard guardrails. The field mapping itself is handled in the central CMS/integration layer (not by store staff); store-level users only see the rendered, rule-selected board. Takeaway: at scale, field mapping is an admin/template-author concern done ONCE centrally; per-location/per-store users must never see a mapping UI — they get inheritance + override. This validates VenueOS's existing district->school tenant-inheritance pattern as the right backbone for multi-location menu rollout. Source: cokesolutions.com Digital Menu Boards: More Than Meets the Eye; qsrmagazine.com / fastcasual.com Freestyle 8100; navori.com QSR; lookdigitalsignage.com; pickcel.com/blog/coca-cola-menu-board; lsquared.com QSR menu boards guide.

products.name: Yodeck DSMenu + DSMenu.com / SmarterSign / DsMenu (template-library menu boards)
products.mappingApproach: Template-first with click-to-edit text fields and an optional data feed. Yodeck's DSMenu widget gives a library of menu-board layouts where the operator edits text directly ('click the Menu Item placeholder text and the price list and type your changes') for fully manual menus, OR connects a data source (Google Sheet / Excel / POS) so menus auto-refresh on data change (DsMenu's 'Automatic Menu Updates'). Yodeck also has an open Toast price-integration feature request — i.e., direct real-time Toast pricing is demanded but was still on the roadmap, illustrating that 'connect any POS' is hard and many vendors start with sheet/CSV bridges before native POS. Takeaway: a two-mode editor — (a) hand-typed placeholders for operators with no POS feed, (b) bind-to-feed for those who have one — covers the whole customer range and is the pragmatic launch shape. Source: yodeck.com/docs DSMenu widget, yodeck.com/solutions/digital-menu-boards, feedback.yodeck.com Toast Menu Pricing Integration, dsmenu.com/Home/POSMenu and /home/HowItWorks.

uxPatterns: Spectrum of mapping visibility (4 tiers): (1) INVISIBLE/no-map — POS-native, the catalog is the schema (Square Kiosk); (2) IMPLICIT/auto-import — connector mirrors the whole POS menu tree, operator only picks which menu/category to surface (Toast/Clover via Menuboard Manager, Wallboard, SmarterSign); (3) OBJECT-DRAG — operator drags whole ITEM objects (carrying all fields) onto a canvas and the system reflows (Menuzen); (4) EXPLICIT per-element binding — operator wires each text/image element to a named data field via a Settings/properties panel (OptiSync, Intuiface). The non-technical sweet spot is tiers 2-3; tier 4 is the power-user fallback when design freedom is required.

Bind ITEMS, not FIELDS. The most usable editors (Menuzen, Square) make the unit of manipulation a first-class menu-item OBJECT that internally knows its name/price/photo/availability — the operator never thinks about 'which field goes where.' Only the data-binding tools (OptiSync) expose field-level mapping, and they need a Repeater + properties panel to keep it sane.

The 'Repeater' / smart-list primitive is universal. Every system that renders a variable-length menu needs a way to design ONE row/tile and have it repeat for N items. OptiSync calls it a Repeater; Menuzen calls it Smart Layouts with Intelligent Item Flow; Square uses fixed category grids. Without it, operators would hand-place every line.

Auto-86 + auto-reflow is the headline feature, and reflow matters as much as the hide. Hiding an out-of-stock item is table stakes (Toast/Clover/Square all do it). Menuzen's differentiator is that it CLOSES THE GAP and reflows the layout so the board never shows a hole — the auto-86 UX is only good if the layout heals itself.

Per-location price resolution from ONE design. Multi-location operators build a single template; the system resolves store-specific pricing/availability from the data source at render time (Menuzen 'Multi-Location Toggler'; enterprise QSR central CMS + franchisee overrides). The operator does NOT duplicate the design per store.

Two-mode editor covers the whole market: (a) hand-typed placeholder text for operators with no POS feed (Yodeck DSMenu click-to-edit), and (b) bind-to-feed auto-refresh for operators who have a POS or a spreadsheet (DsMenu Automatic Menu Updates, OptiSync). Most vendors ship the spreadsheet/CSV bridge BEFORE native POS because POS integrations are slow to build.

Connect step is a guided 6-step linear wizard, not a config screen: Connect -> Import -> Design -> Schedule -> Publish -> Monitor (Wallboard's published flow, mirrored by others). Each step is one decision; the field mapping is absorbed into 'Import' so the operator never sees a mapping table.

Photo handling has a graceful fallback chain. Square: item photo -> if category has none, borrow a child item's photo. The pattern: never show a blank tile — cascade name->photo->category-photo->brand-default so an un-photographed item still renders.

Mapping is an author-once, central-admin concern at scale. In enterprise QSR the person who maps POS fields to the template is a brand/template author who does it ONCE; per-store staff only ever see the finished, rule-selected board (dayparting + inheritance + override). Store users must never be shown a mapping UI.

Dayparting + rules engine sits ON TOP of the POS feed, not inside it. POS drives price/availability; a separate scheduling/rules layer swaps which template/section shows by time-of-day, day, season, weather, and local events — and is what franchisees actually touch.
keyTakeaways: The market has decisively moved AWAY from manual field-by-field mapping. First-party (Square) and dedicated menu vendors (Toast/Clover connectors, Menuzen) expose NO field-mapping UI at all — the operator picks a POS menu/category and the connector mirrors the whole tree. Explicit per-element binding (OptiSync, Intuiface) survives only as the power-user path when full design freedom is required.

Auto-86 with self-healing reflow is the single most-marketed capability and the clearest buying trigger. 'Change the price in your POS, it's on the screen in seconds; sell out, it disappears and the layout closes the gap' is the universal pitch. code.fieldSystem: Widget field system has three layers: (1) Markup layer — widgets mark bindable fields with [data-field] attributes (HS/sports widgets) or export DEFAULTS objects with dot-notation keys (MS pack, Fitness, HS portrait variants). (2) Config layer — templates store cfg as nested JSON; PropertiesPanel auto-generates form fields from DEFAULTS exports. (3) Editing layer — StyleableField (PropertiesPanel.tsx:5343) wraps inputs, dispatches 'template-edit-field' CustomEvent on focus, and PropertiesPanel routes to data-field-section by fieldName. Styles stored in __styles (legacy) or _styles (canonical) FieldStyleMaps. Game state fields (SCORE_HOME, GAME_CLOCK) read via GameStateContext.useGameState() which polls GET /sports/board/:id every 750ms. CTS scoreboard fields (homeScore, awayScore, clock, period, exclusions) consumed via 'edu:cts-game-state' window CustomEvent. POS menu fields (items, categories) read via static config filters (connectionId, category). Currently NO generic field-to-system binding — all mappings are hardcoded in widget render logic.
gaps: NO data-source abstraction: Widgets contain hardcoded knowledge of specific systems (GameState, CTS, POS). No primitive to declare 'this widget accepts data from: [game_state | cts | pos | webhook]' with schema discovery. Would require DataSource service, FieldBinding table, schema registry (DataSourceField) mapping (sourceId, fieldPath, dataType, isArray, updateFrequencyHz).

NO field-binding UI: PropertiesPanel has hard-coded switch cases per widget type listing available fields. No generic editor surfacing all bindable fields, allowing operator to pick a data source + map sourceFieldPath → cfg.fieldName. Would need FieldBindingEditor.tsx, DataSourcePicker.tsx components.

NO generic realtime message type: RealtimeGateway broadcasts only GAME_STATE, EMERGENCY, HEARTBEAT. No FIELD_CHANGED or DATA_FIELD message type for arbitrary field updates from webhooks, POS, or external APIs. Widgets have no subscription mechanism for 'notify me when field X changes from source Y'.

NO webhook-as-data-source: Custom webhook endpoint (POST /api/v1/webhooks) exists but is fire-and-forget audit logging only. Never integrated into template data consumption. Needs schema validation, field extraction, binding resolution, realtime dispatch.

NO field-value resolution at render time: Widgets call GameStateContext.useGameState() or listen to CustomEvents directly. No FieldBindingContext (parallel to GameStateContext) that resolves bound field values from realtime WS, falls back to config, handles source failover/priority.

NO schema discovery UI: Operator cannot browse available fields from a data source (CTS exposes [homeScore, awayScore, clockMs, period, exclusions], GameState exposes [homeScore, awayScore, clockMs, segment, ...], POS exposes [items[].name, items[].price, categories]). Would need source.introspect() API + schema display in FieldBindingEditor.

NO field type validation: Templates accept any JSON in cfg. No schema enforcing cfg.homeScore is a number, cfg.homeAbbrev is max 3 chars, cfg.logoUrl is a URL. A binding system would need TypeScript types (FieldType enum: STRING | NUMBER | BOOLEAN | ARRAY | OBJECT | IMAGE_URL | DATE) + validator functions.

NO field update audit trail: GameEvent logs game mutations (SCORE, SEGMENT, CLOCK, CUE) but not field-data mutations from external sources. A real system needs audit table (sourceId, fieldPath, oldValue, newValue, timestamp, userId, reason) for compliance/debugging.

NO priority/fallback logic: If multiple sources could provide the same field (e.g., homeScore from both CTS and a custom webhook), there is no tie-breaker. No UI to configure source priority, polling frequency, error handling (use last-known value vs. zeroing vs. hiding).

NO offline cache coordination: Player has SW cache + localStorage for playlists/emergency media, but no cache invalidation for field data. A realtime binding system needs to coordinate cache busts when source updates, especially for critical fields (score, clock).
